findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Specify the disjoint-tree case as an explicit algorithmic branch of the NCA walk (e.g., 'if the two chains share no element, treat as having no common ancestor and link unchanged'), so the no-NCA path is a deterministic output of the algorithm rather than a parallel natural-language rule.
evidence: Plan says 'Build the full ancestor chain of each endpoint, find their nearest common ancestor (NCA), and escalate each endpoint to its own ancestor that sits directly below that NCA.' — no branch is defined for when the ancestor chains share no element.

Plan adds separately: 'Tickets with no parent are siblings of one another, so two roots — and two tickets in disjoint trees — link unchanged.' — this is a disjoint natural-language rule, not a consequence of the stated algorithm.
The existing code shows that NCA detection would compare ancestor-chain sets; if source_chain ∩ target_chain is empty the algorithm has no defined output per the plan text.
findings.finding: The NCA algorithm is under-specified for the disjoint-tree case: when two tickets share no common ancestor, 'find their nearest common ancestor' has no output, and the plan handles this only via a separate natural-language rule ('disjoint trees link unchanged') rather than as a defined algorithmic branch. An implementer building the NCA walk may produce undefined behavior (empty intersection, key error, or silent wrong result) on disjoint trees without a spec-level instruction for this branch.
findings.location: Approach section — 'Structural rule (blocking relations)' paragraph; also Testing — 'Happy path: two tickets with no parent'
scenarios: Two tickets whose chains share no element (genuinely disjoint subtrees, not just parentless): the NCA walk finds no shared node and may fall through to an unspecified state, silently promoting to a root or raising an exception.
A parentless ticket linked to a ticket with a deep chain: the plan says 'treat as siblings' but the NCA algorithm as described finds no NCA.
findings.suggested_fix: Add to the Approach section: 'If the ancestor chains share no element (disjoint trees, or either ticket is parentless and they are not the same root), no NCA exists — treat as siblings of one another and link unchanged (was_redirected=False). A chain-root equality check (source_chain[-1] == target_chain[-1]) is a sufficient fast test for a shared root before full intersection.'

evidence: Current code: single `is_redundant` at line 167 used at lines 175 (non-blocking return) and 227 (blocking return).

Scope bullet says: 'compute is_redundant for that branch from the resolved pair as an ancestor-descendant test' — ambiguous whether this replaces or supplements the existing line 167 computation.
findings.finding: The plan specifies two different `is_redundant` semantics for the two branches (non-blocking: direct parent-child on the original pair; blocking: ancestor-descendant on the RESOLVED pair), but the existing code uses a SINGLE shared variable computed once before both branches (line 167). The Scope section says only to 'compute `is_redundant` for that branch from the resolved pair as an ancestor-descendant test' without stating that the shared variable at line 167 must NOT be widened and that a SECOND, separate computation must be added inside the blocking branch after resolution. A reading of the plan that widens the single variable at line 167 would apply ancestor-descendant rejection to non-blocking relations, which the plan explicitly forbids.
findings.location: Approach section — 'Redundancy guard, evaluated post-resolution' paragraph; Scope section — `src/rebar/graph/_hierarchy.py` bullet; code at `src/rebar/graph/_hierarchy.py:163–176`
scenarios: An implementer replaces line 167 with the widened ancestor-descendant predicate evaluated on the original pair — this applies the new rejection to non-blocking relations (e.g., a `relates_to` between a grandparent and grandchild now raises, contradicting AC line 5 and the plan's non-blocking regression spec).

The existing test `test_resolve_hierarchy_link_is_redundant_direct_parent` still passes (direct parent-child satisfies both predicates), masking the regression on non-blocking relations until a broader test is run.
findings.suggested_fix: Add to the `_hierarchy.py` scope bullet: 'Leave the existing `is_redundant` variable at line 167 (direct parent-child, used by the non-blocking early return) unchanged; add a new `blocking_is_redundant` variable computed after NCA resolution — `resolved_source in target_chain or resolved_target in source_chain` — and use this in the blocking branch's return dict.'

findings.finding: The plan's deletion-safety claim states 'The package `__all__` (`src/rebar/graph/__init__.py:28`) re-exports only `resolve_hierarchy_link` and `compute_archive_eligible` from this module, so none of the four is part of the package surface.' But `__init__.py:45` includes `"_hierarchy"` in `__all__`, meaning the entire `_hierarchy` module object is part of the re-exported surface. Any consumer can access `rebar.graph._hierarchy._TYPE_TIER` (and the other three symbols) via the module reference. The four symbols ARE reachable through the package surface.
findings.location: Approach section: 'The package __all__ (src/rebar/graph/__init__.py:28) re-exports only resolve_hierarchy_link and compute_archive_eligible from this module, so none of the four is part of the package surface.'
findings.suggested_fix: Replace 'The package `__all__` … re-exports only `resolve_hierarchy_link` and `compute_archive_eligible` from this module, so none of the four is part of the package surface' with: 'The four are private to `_hierarchy.py` and referenced nowhere else: `grep -rn` for each name across `src/` and `tests/`, excluding `_hierarchy.py` itself, returns no matches. Although `__init__.py:45` includes `_hierarchy` (the submodule) in `__all__`, no caller accesses these symbols through that path.'

findings.finding: The plan asserts 'the package `__all__` (`src/rebar/graph/__init__.py:28`) re-exports **only** `resolve_hierarchy_link` and `compute_archive_eligible` from this module' as the safety basis for concluding the four deleted symbols are not part of the package surface. Reading `__init__.py` lines 28-44 shows `__all__` also includes `'_hierarchy'` (the submodule object itself). Because `_hierarchy` is exported as an attribute of `rebar.graph`, any caller doing `rebar.graph._hierarchy._TYPE_TIER` (or equivalent) could access the deleted symbols via the submodule reference. The deletion-safety claim rests on the stronger (and false) premise that only the two named symbols are exported; the actual guarantee is only that the four names are not directly listed in `__all__`.
findings.location: Approach section — 'Removal is safe because … the package `__all__` (`src/rebar/graph/__init__.py:28`) re-exports only `resolve_hierarchy_link` and `compute_archive_eligible` from this module'
findings.suggested_fix: Replace 'the package `__all__` re-exports only `resolve_hierarchy_link` and `compute_archive_eligible` from this module, so none of the four is part of the package surface' with: 'none of the four names appears in `__all__` directly, and `grep -rn` across `src/` and `tests/` (excluding `_hierarchy.py` itself) returns no matches — the grep evidence alone establishes deletion safety.'

findings.finding: The plan's deletion-safety justification for `_TYPE_TIER` and the tier helpers incorrectly characterises `src/rebar/graph/__init__.py`'s `__all__`. A grep confirms no caller currently exploits this path, so deletion is safe in practice, but the stated justification is factually wrong and could cause a code reviewer to accept an incorrect premise.
findings.location: Approach section — 'They are safe to remove because … not re-exported from src/rebar/graph/__init__.py, whose __all__ (src/rebar/graph/__init__.py:27) exports only resolve_hierarchy_link and compute_archive_eligible from this module'
findings.suggested_fix: Replace: '…not re-exported from src/rebar/graph/__init__.py, whose __all__ (src/rebar/graph/__init__.py:27) exports only resolve_hierarchy_link and compute_archive_eligible from this module.' With: '…not referenced by any caller outside _hierarchy.py: a grep of src/ and tests/ for _TYPE_TIER, _tier_of, _tier_of_ticket, and _promote_to_tier returns only definitions within _hierarchy.py itself. Although src/rebar/graph/__init__.py's __all__ includes the _hierarchy submodule (line 45), no code accesses the tier helpers through that path.'

findings.finding: The plan places the new ancestor-descendant refusal at the END of the blocking branch, but does not resolve the collision with the existing `is_redundant` path for direct-parent-child BLOCKING pairs. A direct parent-child pair (e.g. `story-parent blocks task-child`) is also an ancestor-descendant pair under the new structural rule — the NCA equals one of the endpoints. If the ancestor check fires and returns `{"error":...}`, the existing test `test_resolve_hierarchy_link_is_redundant_direct_parent` (which calls `resolve_hierarchy_link` with the default `blocks` relation and asserts `result['is_redundant'] is True`) will receive an error dict instead, and `test_add_dependency_redundant_link_exits_nonzero` (which matches `'redundant'` in the ValueError message) will get an ancestor-descendant message instead. AC#4 claims `is_redundant` 'still reports only the direct parent-child case', but this is only true for non-blocking relations under the new design — it silently stops being true for blocking direct-parent-child pairs.
findings.location: Approach section ('The resolver already has two distinct rejection channels'); AC#4; src/rebar/graph/_hierarchy.py:167
findings.suggested_fix: The simplest fix is to keep `is_redundant` as the short-circuit for direct-parent-child pairs for ALL relations (blocking and non-blocking) by moving the ancestor-descendant check after the is_redundant guard, or by documenting that the existing `test_resolve_hierarchy_link_is_redundant_direct_parent` and `test_add_dependency_redundant_link_exits_nonzero` are updated to expect the new ancestor-descendant error path. Either is valid, but the plan must pick one explicitly.
